title: Ten Forward Talent Night
subtitle: U.S.S. Enterprise NCC-1701-D, stardate 44390.7
author: personal recording, name withheld
extra: Dubbed from the Archive copy. Sixty-eight years old.

lines.text: PERSONAL RECORDING. DO NOT ARCHIVE.
TEN FORWARD, DECK TEN: STARDATE 44390.7
The television is a surface artifact. I logged it as one.
Then I found out what else it plays, and here we are.
Sixty-eight years old, and nobody has watched this.
The camera is on a table at the back. Nobody adjusts it.
Ladies, gentlemen, others: Ten Forward Talent Night.
House rules. No phasers, no holograms, no encores.
Somebody at the bar says NO ENCORES again, louder.
First up. Commander Riker, on the trumpet.
Trombone.
On the trombone. Commander Riker.
Four minutes of trombone. It is genuinely good.
Seven minutes of trombone. It is still genuinely good.
Nine. The bar has quietly started serving again.
Will. Will. There are seventeen acts.
Thank you, Commander. Thank you. Commander.
Lieutenant Commander Data. Reading his own work.
He announces eighteen stanzas. He is not joking.
Stanza four is about the cat's indifference to poetry.
Stanza eleven is about the cat's indifference to him.
By fourteen the room has stopped finding it funny.
By eighteen they are applauding, and they mean it.
Doctor Crusher. Who has done this professionally.
She taps. The deck is not sprung. She does not care.
Lieutenant Worf has declined to participate.
He has not declined. He has been entered.
A long silence. Then forty seconds of Klingon opera.
Nobody in the room breathes through any of it.
...Mister Worf, that was extraordin...
I have declined to participate.
Ensign Ruiz. Impressions of the senior staff.
Engineering, security, medical. Cruel and exact.
He starts on the captain. He is eleven words in.
He looks at table six. The captain is at table six.
Do go on, Ensign.
He does not go on. He sits down. They are merciless.
Lieutenant Barclay is on the list and not in the room.
RECORDING CONTINUES
The room empties. Nobody switches the camera off.
Two people stack chairs and argue about the trombone.
I watch the end more than the acts. The chair stacking.
There are nineteen more. Start with this one.
